name: Live Region
summary: How a page says something out loud — role="status" against role="alert", an announcer for messages that belong to no element, and the three ways a region ends up silent with all the right text in the DOM.
demoNote: The regions are drawn as visible boxes so you can watch text land in them; in an app they would be clipped. Example 3 is broken on purpose and live — all three buttons leave the right text in the DOM and none of them announces anything, which is why this bug survives code review. Turn on a screen reader for this page.

contract.useWhen: Announcing a change, to a region that was already being listened to.
failureModes: the region injected already holding its text, so nothing changed after it was observed
display:none on the region, which is not in the tree to change
cleared and set in the same tick, which is reported as one state
one requestAnimationFrame — it runs before paint, so both writes still batch
aria-live written by hand instead of the role, losing aria-atomic and the name
assertive for anything merely important, rather than for what stops being useful in seconds
